question: A tradesman marked his goods at 26% above its cost price and then allowed a discount of 13%. His gain (in %) is:
solution:
**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹100 (Assume)

Marked Price (MP) = CP + 26% of CP

Discount = 13%

**Formula used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP - Discount

Profit Percentage = dfrac{SP - CP}{CP} times 100

**Calculation:**

MP = 100 + 26% of 100

⇒ MP = 100 + 26

⇒ MP = 126

Discount = 13% of 126

⇒ Discount = dfrac{13}{100} times 126 

⇒ Discount = 16.38

SP = MP - Discount

⇒ SP = 126 - 16.38

⇒ SP = 109.62

Profit Percentage = dfrac{SP - CP}{CP} times 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = dfrac{109.62 - 100}{100} times 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = dfrac{9.62}{100} times 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = 9.62%

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**
